I learned a lot while researching for this project specifically that some microcontrollers have better capabilities when connecting to your computer like keyboard. So I did research on which ones were the cheapest that had those capabilities, and I found the raspberry pie pico, to be the best. I then took a bunch of measurements, and came up with a plan of kind of how big I want the button to be and how big it had to be based off of the size of the pico. And I did a bunch of research of how to code the button. So it was able to launch portal on my computer. Unfortunately, I can't make it directly. Launch portal, but I found out that if I make a key shortcut on my computer that launches portal and then code the button to press those same buttons it should work.

The session is kind of a bunch of days put together, first of all, I made the portal button I used onshape to cad it. Giving an organic looking kind of decorative shape is pretty hard on onshape, but I was able to do it fine it just took me a while longer. Then, I painted the model in bamboo lab. This was the first time i've ever painted a model to be different colors. If you look at the lines between the different pieces on the portal button, they aren't the cleanest. I printed out the portal button. Because I was really curious how well my door was gonna work. And how well the button was going to fit into it, but it fits fine. Everything works well. Then, I put a shortcut to portal 2 on my computer and then set shortcut keys for it too, lastly, I encoded the button I wrote the code just straight and github. I am assuming that's not the best way to do it, but that's what I did. Basically, the code says. When the button is pressed, then it will press the buttons that I set as a shortcut. All at the same time so then that should trigger the shortcut. And then launch the game.
